Returns render id, absolute file paths, size, lint summary and metrics (fonts, colours, libs). Never returns image bytes unless include_images=true. A page already written to disk goes as path, not pasted into html.

name: design_lint
description:
Deterministic design checks on HTML/URL (fonts, contrast, motion, a11y, generic-AI patterns). Lint de diseño.
Every rule is a row of data with a stable id (design_rules_list): core, slop, quality, craft and, with tokens_id, ds/* against a design system. Each finding has area, severity, tier (floor/reflex/finish), evidence and a concrete fix.
Sinónimos: lint, revisar diseño, patrones genéricos de IA, contraste, accesibilidad.

name: design_critique
description:
Critique a rendered page: score 0-10, findings with fixes, using lint + local vision model. Crítica de diseño.
Merges deterministic lint with an optional vision-model rubric (hierarchy, typography, colour, motion, a11y, copy). Tiers: Floor errors always block, Reflex warnings block unless waived on the record (waivers=[{rule, reason}], reason 24+ characters, never repeated), Finish advisories never block. gate.state is pass or fix. clean_review=true adds a fresh-context verdict: recapture, rebuild, fix or ship.
Sinónimos: criticar, evaluar diseño, puntuación, feedback visual.

clean_review.description: Final review in a clean context: a fresh call to the global model with only the screenshots, the HTML and the findings. The verdict (recapture | rebuild | fix | ship) comes first; at most 8 findings.

Explicit criteria verify requested effects; generic coverage cannot infer every intended effect. Takes ~15-60 s.

Statically checks a snippet against the libraries installed in the environment:

too many positional arguments, missing required arguments, deprecated calls. Never runs

name: api_upgrade_rehearsal
description:
Rehearse a package upgrade on a project (upgrade rehearsal, comprobar actualización)

Indexes the package's current and target versions (the target is installed with pip into an
isolated temp folder - never into the project's environment), diffs the API surface
(removed symbols, changed signatures, moved modules), finds every use in the project and
classifies it: broken (removed, or the call no longer fits), at risk (default changed,
deprecated, behaviour change documented in the docstring/changelog) or ok. Proposes exact
file:line edits only where they are mechanical (renamed keyword, moved import with one
certain new home) and lists the rest as manual. With run_tests it applies the edits to a
throwaway copy and runs the test command with the old and the new version to report
regressions. The project itself is never edited. Python projects only.

Args:
    project_path: absolute path of the project folder.
    package: distribution name (as in requirements).
    target_version: version to rehearse.
    old_version: current version if it is not installed in the project's environment.
    old_path / new_path: use these source folders instead of the installed / pip-installed trees (offline use).
    run_tests: run the before/after test comparison in throwaway copies (default true).
    test_command: e.g. "python -m pytest -q"; default pytest when the project has test files.

Returns: {summary: {verdict, broken, at_risk, ok, ...}, api_diff, uses: {broken, at_risk, ok_count},
    plan: {mechanical_edits: [{file, line, col, old, new, reason}], manual, diff}, tests: {before, after,
    after_edits, regressions, fixed_by_edits}, limitations}.
Keywords: upgrade, dependency, bump version, migration plan, breaking changes, changelog, actualizar

Compares each target locale against source_locale; complex ICU-style messages
are counted as unchecked rather than claimed valid. Never edits a catalogue.

Args:
    path: absolute path to the directory containing en.json, es.json, etc.
    source_locale: source file stem, default en.
    offset: finding offset for the next page.
    limit: findings per page, at most 100.

Returns: {source_locale, locales, source_keys, total, unchecked_messages,
    findings: [{locale, key, kind, expected?, actual?}], truncated,
    has_more, next_offset}.
Keywords: translation audit, localization keys, placeholder mismatch, i18n,
    comprobar traducciones, claves faltantes, variables de traducción, idiomas

Inspector/CDP metadata never evaluates, pauses or closes the target; script text, page DOM/listeners, completed response bodies and PNG are explicit choices. Device actions and instrumentation scripts can change their targets. Captures are historical, not behavioral equivalence; cancellation cannot undo effects. Remote tokens are ephemeral and excluded from recordings.

name: theseus_project_create

name: theseus_project_read

name: theseus_project_update

name: theseus_artifact_add

name: theseus_analysis_catalog

name: theseus_analysis_start

Caller-selected commands may execute code, mutate files, access the network and read external inputs; retained readers do not replay commands.

name: theseus_analysis_records

name: theseus_binary_close
description: Close a native binary session and save its retained analysis project. Returns a background close job.

name: theseus_binary_compare
description: Compare selected functions from two open native sessions, including exact referenced data bytes. Normalize only proven decoder address fields; unresolved boundaries remain unknown. Returns a persistent job, not a behavioral equivalence proof.

name: theseus_workflow_read
description: Read reconstruction obligations, unresolved questions, evidence freshness, behavior handoffs and oracle sensitivity results. Completion is derived from observations, not an editable pass flag.

name: theseus_claim_save

name: theseus_handoff_read
description: Read a saved immutable handoff; builder_only returns only the behavior document, without reader findings/artifact paths.

name: theseus_oracle_selftest
description: Test deliberately wrong commands or explicitly mapped retained page/process captures, one capture per selected scenario. Reports detected, surviving and invalid observations. Retained tests never connect or replay; incomplete, changed or unaligned captures cannot certify sensitivity.

name: theseus_reconstruction_verify
description: Run saved differential scenarios linked to an immutable behavior handoff. Each retry preserves the original handoff identity and complete observations; a newer specification is explicitly reported.

name: theseus_equivalence_suite_save
description: Save an equivalence suite: reference and candidate commands (argv, cwd, env, timeout) plus cases (stdin, args, input files for a fresh sandbox, optional SQLite seed, multi-step sequences), explicit opt-in normalisers, authorized deviations and seeded generators (integers, decimals, strings, permutations). Suite de equivalencia.

name: theseus_equivalence_suite_read
description: Read one saved equivalence suite, or list the project's suites when suite_id is omitted.

name: theseus_equivalence_run
description: Run a saved or inline equivalence suite as a background job. Both programs run on identical fresh sandboxes; exit code, stdout, stderr, file effects and SQLite state are compared per step. Reports the first disagreement per case, authorized deviations separately, a constant-candidate strength check (weak suites are flagged) and shrinks generated failing inputs by re-running both programs. Read the job with theseus_job_read. Agreement covers only the listed cases and channels; it is not whole-program equivalence. Comprobar equivalencia.

name: theseus_rules_save
description: Save or update a business rule extracted from a legacy program: statement in the user's vocabulary, code evidence (artifact/file, lines, function), examples, counterexamples and an optional executable check (safe predicate over case input and the reference program's output, plus cases/generators). New rules are always hypotheses; only theseus_rules_check changes status. Banco de reglas.

check.description: {reference:{argv,cwd,env,timeout_seconds}, predicate, when, cases:[equivalence cases], generators:[equivalence generators]}. predicate/when use a safe expression language over stdin, args, files, exit_code, stdout, stderr, output_files, steps, value, index (comparisons, arithmetic, string and regex helpers, round_half_up/round_half_even; no attribute access, imports or arbitrary calls).

name: theseus_rules_read
description: Read one rule with evidence, history and last check, or list the project's rules with status counts when rule_id is omitted.

name: theseus_rules_check
description: Run a rule's check as a background job: the reference program runs on generated and listed cases in fresh sandboxes and the predicate is evaluated. hypothesis becomes observed only if every applicable case holds; the first contradicting case is shrunk by re-running the program and the rule becomes contradicted. Status changes are kept in the rule history. Observed is evidence on the executed cases, not proof. Read the job with theseus_job_read.

name: theseus_rules_export
description: Export the rules bank (optionally filtered by ids or statuses) as client-ready Markdown: statement, status, code evidence, examples and counterexample per rule.

name: theseus_property_run
description: Run a property and business-sequence suite as a background job. A target program (argv command or a Python callable 'module:function' in a subprocess) is driven by seeded, composable input strategies (integers, decimals, text, lists, dicts, one_of, tuples) and checked against properties written in the safe expression language: invariants, round trips (export then import), idempotence f(f(x))==f(x), metamorphic relations and reference-model comparisons. Stateful suites execute random command sequences (with preconditions, a model updated by expressions and postconditions) against the real program in one sandbox. Failures are shrunk by re-executing every candidate and keeping the same violated property; the minimal case is returned. Oracles that only compare the program with itself are warned about. No counterexample found is evidence on the executed runs, not a proof. Read the job with theseus_job_read.

suite.description: {target:{argv|callable,path,encode,decode}, input:<strategy>, runs, seed, properties:[{kind:invariant|roundtrip|idempotent|metamorphic|model, name, when, expr, then, transform, reference, input}], stateful:[{name, program, init, files, db, commands:[{name,args,stdin,params,pre,update,post}], runs, max_length, seed}]}

name: theseus_synthesize
description: Synthesize a business rule as a safe expression from input/output examples (and outputs it must not produce) as a background job: enumerative search by size with observational-equivalence pruning over arithmetic, comparisons, conditionals, rounding functions and string operations, then a counterexample-guided loop that validates the simplest consistent expression against a reference program on generated and boundary inputs, turning every disagreement into a new example. Returns the expression, the examples used, the validation coverage and, on failure, the closest candidates with their counterexamples. save_rule stores the expression as a hypothesis in the rules bank (status changes only through theseus_rules_check). Read the job with theseus_job_read.

rejected.description: [{input:{x:10}, output:99}]: outputs the expression must not produce for that input

reference.description: {argv|callable, path, encode: text|json|json_object, decode: auto|json|text, cwd, env, timeout_seconds}

domain.description: {variable: input strategy} used to generate validation inputs

name: theseus_repro_create
description: Reproduce a reported failure in a fresh sandbox, confirm it twice, then minimise stdin, input files and env vars by delta debugging, re-executing and keeping the same failure signature at every step (a different failure is never accepted). Writes a repro bundle directory (inputs, run.sh, run.cmd, expected signature, environment fingerprint) and returns a background job. Reproducir fallo.

report.description: {command:{argv,cwd,env,timeout_seconds}, stdin, files:{path:text|{base64}}, env:{name:value}, description, expected_predicate (true when output is correct), signature:{exit_code|'nonzero', stderr_regex, stdout_regex, timed_out, predicate}}

name: theseus_repro_verify
description: Run a repro bundle (by bundle_dir or the repro job id) against the recorded program or an override argv such as a fixed version, and report reproduces or no_longer_reproduces plus environment differences. Verificar reproduccion.

name: theseus_stateful_recipe_save
description: Save (or revise with recipe_id) a stateful HTTP sequence recipe for a real test service: target command started on a free port in a fresh sandbox per run ({python}, {sandbox}, {port} placeholders) or a base_url with a reset request; a model of named variables; actions with explicit preconditions, seeded parameter strategies, picks of identifiers bound by earlier responses (by index, or by the step that produced them as {from: step id, var: extractor}; re-bound on replay), request template, accepted statuses, extractors, model updates and postconditions; invariants over the model and declared read-only SQLite queries (watch.sqlite + queries); optional authorised reference target with agree relations. Oracles are written by you in the safe expression language; nothing is inferred from endpoint names. Receta de secuencias con estado.

lang.description: Language of human-readable text (default en); machine fields are unchanged.

recipe.description: {name, target:{argv,env,port_env,ready,files,db}|{base_url,reset}, reference, model:{var:init}, setup:[{request,expect_status,extract}], actions:[{name,pre,params:{p:<strategy>},pick:{name:list_var},request:{method,path,headers,body},expect_status,extract:{local:expr},update:{var:expr},post:[{name,expr,explain}],agree:[...]}], invariants:[{name,expr}], watch:{sqlite,tables,files}, queries:{name:SELECT}, server_errors_fail, runs, max_length, seed}

name: theseus_stateful_recipe_read
description: Read one stateful recipe (with revision) or list the project's recipes when recipe_id is omitted.

lang.description: Language of human-readable text (default en); machine fields are unchanged.

name: theseus_stateful_run
description: Run a stateful recipe as a background job: each run restarts the target with fresh state, generates a seeded sequence online (only actions whose precondition holds on the live model), executes it against the real service and checks status expectations, extractors, postconditions, invariants (HTTP, SQLite and file effects are reported separately) and reference relations. The first failing sequence is reduced by delta debugging plus parameter shrinking, re-executing every candidate on a fresh process, keeping preconditions valid and the same (action, kind, oracle) signature. Setup failures are inconclusive, never passes. Returns coverage per action and transition, including what never ran. Read with theseus_job_read.

lang.description: Language of human-readable text (default en); machine fields are unchanged.

name: theseus_stateful_replay
description: Replay the minimal (or original) counterexample of a stateful run, or an explicit symbolic sequence, on a fresh target; optionally against another version (target override: argv or base_url) or with a reference. Identifiers are re-bound from that target's own responses, never carried over. Reports outcome, whether the original signature reproduces, the trace with HTTP responses and SQLite/file effects, and the identifiers observed.

lang.description: Language of human-readable text (default en); machine fields are unchanged.

name: theseus_stateful_export
description: Export the reduced counterexample of a stateful run as a standalone pytest regression: test file, regression.json (recipe, symbolic sequence, signature), the executor adapter and the expression evaluator, standard library only. It starts the target, replays the sequence and asserts every oracle, so it fails on the defective version and passes on a fixed one (THESEUS_TARGET_ARGV or THESEUS_TARGET_URL select the version). Runs without Theseus, network or a language model.

lang.description: Language of human-readable text (default en); machine fields are unchanged.

name: theseus_perf_profile
description: Causal performance profile of one operation (a command, or an HTTP request against a server it starts) under controlled repetitions: warm-up, N runs, identical inputs, fresh sandbox per run. Python commands run under cProfile; self time is attributed to database/SQL, serialization, rendering, network I/O, model/inference calls (functions matching model_functions patterns), waiting, CPU in user code and other, with median and p90 across runs, the dominant category named first and top hotspots with file:line. Wall-clock segments come from separate unprofiled runs. Background job; read it with theseus_job_read. Perfil de rendimiento.

description: Before/after performance comparison of two versions (two commands, or two directories or git commits copied to temp folders) on the same input: interleaved runs, per-category and total change with a Mann-Whitney U test and a bootstrap interval, and an output check with the equivalence runner (exit code, stdout, stderr, files, SQLite; HTTP status and body). A speed-up that changes results is reported as failed. Background job; read it with theseus_job_read. Comparar rendimiento.
